title: The weather was wired to the rarest event on the calendar, the ground had no memory, and a citizen was the same size as a crate

verified.THE WEATHER, from the run's own numbers: climate.storm_intensity is 0.000 on ALL 450 rows; climate.weather reads 'snowfall' for ~7000 of those ticks with wind 0.22-0.31 and visibility down to 0.83. The ground shader's `storm` uniform was driven off storm_intensity() — [P09]'s Great Frost envelope — so every hour a critic has ever looked at was an hour with snow falling and a plain rendered dead calm. LcnWorldModel.ground_weather() now composes kind x intensity x wind with the frost as the TOP of the same scale.
verified.NEW frame-lab plate 'snow' (a stub clima: changes 9.4% of the frame, mean |delta| 0.0058, ground told 0.30 (floors 4.5% / 0.0025)
verified.the same snow plate against the pre-chan: 0.0% of the frame, mean |delta| 0.0000, ground told 0.00 — EXACTLY zero. Two named FAILs.
verified.the blizzard plate, unchanged in intent: 74-75% of the frame, mean |delta| 0.020 (was 48.3% before the clock was frozen for the beat; both far above the 10% floor)
verified.THE GROUND'S MEMORY: a sixth data field: NEW frame-lab beat 'wear': the same camera, the same frozen hour, the people HIDDEN IN BOTH PLATES, 260 ticks of walking between them. 1707 footfalls change 8.42% of the screen, mean |delta| 0.0088 (floors 4.0% / 0.0035).
verified.the same wear beat against HEAD~1: 0 footfalls, 0.19% of the frame, mean |delta| 0.0001, field mean 0.00000. Two named FAILs.
verified.and the wear response curve was measured: at weight 12 the beat scored 0.37%, at 16 it scored 1.13% — and at BOTH the fresh and lived plates were indistinguishable held side by side in the crop. A number above zero is not a picture. The floors are set where a human can see it.

The floor is now a curve (applied to the smallest thing that walks, everything heavier keeps a compressed share of its size). Heights spread 24/25/26/26/28/30/32/32/33/34/43 px and the worst pair is breaker vs the_long_cold at 0.624, under the 0.66 bar.

open: THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST, and it is not mine to fix: THE POPULATION DOES NOT WALK. The wear field is written from real movement, and in a real first_night run there is almost none. artifacts/F4b_vis, 21600 ticks (18 minutes of game time), 18-26 citizens on screen: SIXTY-TWO footfalls total. The frame lab's preview crowd of 46 lays 1707 in 260 ticks. A footfall is 11 px of travel, so the entire population of the city moved about 700 px in eighteen minutes. That is the critic's 'the city will not staff itself' and the judge's 'nobody is visibly going anywhere' as one number, and it is now printed on every render frame line ('wear 0.00008 over 62 footfalls') so nobody has to take my word for it. [P05] citizens: until people walk between the jobs they hold, the boot marks, the wear field and the four role silhouettes are all drawing an empty stage correctly.

[P05] citizens: agents_for_view() still publishes kind = worker-if-employed else citizen, so two of the four drawn roles (porter, soldier) never appear in a real run. LcnWorldModel reads an OPTIONAL `role` key and maps it straight to the figure. One extra key on a dictionary [P05] already builds. Contract documented at the top of game/view/render/world_model.gd.

INTEGRATOR / game/boot.gd: the opening settlement is STILL mirror-symmetric — look at artifacts/F4b_vis/shots/third_day_city.world.png and the city folds down its own centre line. That is `opening_commands()` in boot.gd, not [P13]'s. I unfolded the preview settlement last wave (tests/render/test_preview_world.gd::test_the_street_plan_does_not_fold_in_half) and that test ports directly to the real opening. It is the cheapest remaining point on 'looks decided rather than generated'.

The wear beat costs 260 extra frames in the frame lab (about a minute on an idle box, several on a loaded one). If tools/check.sh gets tight, WEAR_TICKS is the knob — but lowering it lowers the measured reach, and the floors were set against 260.
[P14] vfx: the snow and storm plates HIDE the vfx layers on purpose, so what is graded is [P13]'s ground. Ground spindrift plus air flakes is the shipping look and nothing measures the combination.

Perf was measured on four cores shared with three other agents' Godot processes. Draw-call counts, pixel grades and silhouette overlaps are load-independent and are the numbers quoted above; the millisecond figures are not, and only the integrator's single-run measurement should be trusted.

tools/check.sh was NOT run to completion in this session. What was run: the full render suite headless (63/63), the frame lab under xvfb at 1920x1080 (full matrix plus five beats), the same frame lab against HEAD~1 in a scratch worktree, tools/determinism.sh, and tools/run_visual.sh.
